function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.content:
It depends on exactly what you mean by “how far” – horizontal distance, vertical height, or the total path length.  
Here’s how each one is computed for a projectile launched from the ground with speed \(v\) at launch angle \(\theta\):

| Quantity | Formula |
|----------|---------|
| **Horizontal distance after time \(t\)** | \(x(t)=v\,\cos\theta \; t\) |
| **Vertical height after time \(t\)** | \(y(t)=v\,\sin\theta \; t-\frac12 g t^{2}\) |
| **Total distance travelled along the path after time \(t\)** | \(s(t)=\sqrt{[v\,\cos\theta \; t]^{2}+[v\,\sin\theta \; t-\tfrac12 g t^{2}]^{2}}\) |
| **Range (horizontal distance when the projectile lands back on the ground)** | \(R=\dfrac{v^{2}\,\sin(2\theta)}{g}\) |

*Assumptions:*  
- No air resistance.  
- Gravitational acceleration \(g\approx 9.81~\text{m/s}^{2}\).  
- Angles measured in radians unless otherwise specified.

If you give me specific numerical values for \(v\), \(\theta\), and \(t\) (and whether you want the horizontal range or the total path length), I can plug them into the appropriate formula and give you a concrete result.
